skill.name: golang-swagger
skill.description: Create and maintain Go OpenAPI documentation with swaggo/swag. Use annotations, generated specifications, Swagger UI integrations, security definitions, and struct tags across common Go web frameworks.
skill.summary: Create accurate, maintainable Swagger documentation for Go APIs with swaggo annotations and generation workflows.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All 89 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation URLs, Go annotations, evaluation text, or tool metadata rather than executable threats. Review of the three scanned files found no prompt-injection text, unauthorized network behavior, or data-exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples can trigger generic shell and URL detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples, annotation syntax, and reference URLs clearly confined to documentation and evaluation text.

remediation.issue: Generated Swagger UI can expose protected API details if enabled without access controls.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict production Swagger UI with authentication or disable the route outside development environments.

content.value_statement: Go API annotations often become incomplete, inconsistent, or difficult to generate. This skill guides accurate OpenAPI documentation, Swagger UI wiring, and schema generation with swaggo.
actual_capabilities: Add and refine swaggo annotations for endpoints, parameters, responses, tags, and security requirements.
Configure swag generation and connect generated documentation to Gin, Echo, Fiber, Chi, or net/http applications.
Model maps, envelopes, generics, time values, byte slices, enums, examples, and field constraints for accurate schemas.
Define Bearer, API key, Basic, and OAuth2 security schemes in the generated OpenAPI documentation.
Diagnose common generation errors, stale documentation, missing imports, and incorrect annotation placement.
limitations: It documents API behavior but does not implement handlers, authentication, authorization, or business logic.
Generated schemas depend on the installed swag version, project layout, framework integration, and source annotations.
It does not replace security testing or verify that documented responses match runtime behavior.
Production Swagger UI access control must be designed and implemented by the application team.

use_cases.title: Document a New Go API
use_cases.description: Create endpoint annotations, response schemas, and a generated Swagger UI for a new Go service.

use_cases.title: Repair an Existing Specification
use_cases.description: Find annotation gaps, stale generated files, invalid response types, and missing security requirements.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Documentation
use_cases.description: Apply consistent schemas, naming, constraints, examples, and framework wiring across multiple Go services.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Endpoint Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Document this Go endpoint with a summary, parameters, success response, failure response, and route annotation. Explain where each comment belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Wire Swagger UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect generated swag documentation to my Go framework and explain the required imports, route registration, generation command, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Model Complex Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this API schema for nested response data, map values, timestamps, byte fields, enums, examples, and validation constraints. Identify unsupported patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit API Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go service documentation for missing routes, inaccurate schemas, inconsistent annotations, stale generated files, and missing security requirements. Return prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: A Gin service has generated docs, but Swagger UI displays an empty specification.
output_examples.output: The fix is to register the generated docs package with a blank import, mount the Gin Swagger handler, regenerate the specification, and verify the route.

output_examples.input: An endpoint returns a response envelope whose data field contains a user object.
output_examples.output: The documentation should use nested response composition so the generated schema shows the concrete user model inside the envelope.

output_examples.input: A user model needs documented roles, score limits, examples, and a hidden secret field.
output_examples.output: Use struct tags for allowed values, numeric bounds, example values, and Swagger-only exclusion while preserving required JSON serialization.

best_practices: Regenerate documentation after annotation or model changes, then review the generated schema for accuracy.
Keep security definitions and endpoint requirements explicit, consistent, and aligned with deployed authentication.
Use named response types and focused annotations when generic maps or envelopes would produce ambiguous schemas.
anti_patterns: Do not publish stale generated documentation that differs from current handlers or models.
Do not hide fields with JSON exclusion when the application still needs to serialize them.
Do not expose production Swagger UI without authentication, authorization, or an intentional deployment policy.

faq.question: Which Go frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Gin, Echo, Fiber, Chi, and net/http integrations supported by the swaggo ecosystem.

faq.question: Does this skill generate the OpenAPI files?
faq.answer: It explains how to configure and run swag generation, but your project environment must provide the swag command.

faq.question: Can it document authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe Bearer, API key, Basic, and OAuth2 schemes and apply security requirements to endpoints.

faq.question: How does it handle fields that Swagger should hide?
faq.answer: Use Swagger-specific exclusion tags when a field must remain available to the application serializer.

faq.question: Can it document generic or nested responses?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides named models, nested composition, and supported generic response notation for clearer schemas.

faq.question: Does it test the API implementation?
faq.answer: No. It improves documentation and generation, but separate tests must verify runtime responses and access controls.
